preview: Mounil Shah shares his placement experience at FinIQ, detailing the group discussion, pseudo-coding round, technical interview, personality round, and final HR round.
content: FinIQ Interview Experience MOUNIL SHAH COMPUTER ENGINEERING, Batch of '22 Before 2021, FinIQ had never visited VJTI, neither for placements nor internships. Prior to the interviews, I had asked around about them and I came to know that their placement process is different every year. Nevertheless, I hope you get some insight from this. The company allowed students from Comps, EXTC and IT departments to apply. They asked for our resumes and based on that, 35 students were shortlisted for the interview process. Round 1 The first round began at 10AM. Group Discussion All the students were divided into four groups, each group having 6-9 students. Upon joining the meet, we were asked to introduce ourselves. A few seconds were given for us to gather our thoughts. Due to time constraints, they had decided to allow each candidate to speak for around 30 seconds on the given topics. We were asked to speak in turns and each person would get one turn to speak. After we were done speaking about the first topic, they gave us another one. Topics for the GD: 1. Keeping poverty as the priority issue, which administration system is the best to deal with it – monarchy, single party system or multi party system? 2. Out of bioweapons and global warming, which one is worse? The entire round lasted for around 20-30 minutes. Tips: Whatever you say, make sure that it makes sense. We received an email at around 12PM regarding the candidates who were shortlisted for the coding round. We were all asked to join the meet for further instructions. Round 2 Coding round We were given three coding questions and were asked to write pseudo code for each of them. After writing the code on paper, we were supposed to scan and send it to one of the employees. We were free to make any assumptions regarding the use of STL, library functions and format of input data. However, whatever assumptions we made, we were supposed to be written. One hour was given for this round. Questions 1. Find the sum of all the non-prime and non-square numbers from 1-1000 2. In a football tournament having 20 teams, each team plays every other team twice – once on their home ground and once away. 'W', 'L' and 'D' represent win (+3 points), loss (+0) and draw (+1 to both) respectively. Let the result of each match be represented as result[A][B] = 'W' where the match is played between teams A and B, on the homeground of A and team A has won the match. Find the team having the highest points. 3. Given the fate of a ball, find the runs scored in one legitimate over. 'N' and 'W' stand for no ball and wide ball respectively Input represents the kind of ball and the runs scored on that ball. Eg: ['N', 4] implies 4 runs are scored on a no ball. We were free to make further assumptions about the input that would be provided. We received an email at around 2:15 wherein they gave a schedule for the 'technical' and 'personality' rounds of all candidates. All those selected for the coding round were required to appear for these two rounds as well. These two rounds were at a gap of one hour from each other. Technical round There were two interviewers in this round. I was asked to explain the code which I had written for all the three questions. There was some cross questioning based on the code. They were interested in the approach used and if I fully understood what I had written. This round lasted for around 30 minutes. Personality round The interviewer started by asking me about myself and my family. Then he asked me about how I liked to spend my free time. I said that I liked chess, listening to music, watching TV series and movies. Apart from that, I also had an interest in national and international politics and finance. He then focused on what exactly did I know about the finance world and I answered by saying that I wasn't exactly interested in the stock market but on how different companies take decisions keeping in mind the effect of those decisions on their share prices. I gave the example of SpaceX. Then he asked me regarding the current news. The date of the interview was 16th August, 2021. I told him about the ongoing India-England test match at Lord's, Prime Minister Modi's speech on Independence Day and how he highlighted the importance of sports, and also talked about how, on the previous day, the Taliban had captured Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan. He then asked my opinion on what the consequences would be if the Taliban was able to take absolute control of the country. The round lasted for around 30-40 minutes. At the end, he asked me if I had any questions. I asked some questions regarding the company and the culture and he answered them. HR round At around 6:30PM, we got a message from our TPO CR that Yash and I had been called for the HR round. I joined the meet. I was asked about how my day was and my experience regarding the interview process. After that, one of the interviewers said that they would be sharing the screen and showing me the compensation breakdown. If I had any doubts, I may ask. 5-10 minutes into this, I asked them if I had been selected for the job. They said,” Yes. Yash and you are the only people which we have selected for the job. This is your salary discussion.” And that is when I realised that my job hunt was finally over. At the end they said that I was assigned the Mumbai office and they would mail us the final offer by night. It was a long day, but it was worth it. Tips: - Prepare well - Be patient - And be confident.
